_note: PLACEHOLDER thresholds for a prototype. Replace each with values cited from NASA HRP / clinical sources and fill in 'source'. Not medical advice.

indicators.label: Heart rate
indicators.how: Place two fingers on your wrist or use the wearable. Rest 5 minutes first.
indicators.why: Microgravity shifts fluids and deconditions the heart; resting HR trends show cardiovascular adaptation.

action.yellow: Hydrate and do light exercise; recheck in 1 hour.
action.red: Stop activity, notify crew medical officer and flight surgeon.

indicators.label: Blood pressure (systolic)
indicators.how: Use the cuff on the upper arm, seated and relaxed.
indicators.why: Fluid shifts and reduced activity change blood pressure regulation.

action.yellow: Recheck after 10 minutes of rest; log symptoms.

indicators.label: Blood glucose
indicators.why: Stress, diet changes and inactivity affect metabolism and nutrition.

indicators.label: Body temperature
indicators.how: Use the forehead or ear thermometer.
indicators.why: Immune changes in spaceflight can mask or trigger infections.

indicators.label: Sleep
indicators.how: From the wearable or a morning log.
indicators.why: Isolation, light cycles and noise disrupt circadian rhythm; poor sleep raises error risk.

action.yellow: Keep a fixed sleep schedule; reduce evening light.
action.red: Report fatigue to crew and flight surgeon.

indicators.label: Mood (1-10)
indicators.how: Self-rating; honest answers matter more than high ones.
indicators.why: Isolation and confinement raise behavioral health risks.

action.yellow: Schedule a call with family or a counselor.
action.red: Request a private conference with ground support.
